_comment: Vocabulary the fetch adapters match against, kept out of the code so a new sender, ESP or locale is a data edit. Structure stays in code: the separators, the repetition, the ordering of forward-then-reply. Matching is case-insensitive, so list each token once in its usual casing. Every `host` here matches that host or any subdomain of it.
_comment_links: What makes a link in a newsletter something other than the article. reject_host_patterns are regexes because these hosts are numbered (campaign-archive1, 2, ...); everything else is a plain list. A share entry needs both a host and how its share path looks, and the two path keys are not interchangeable: path_contains is a substring, path_segment_prefix matches the path exactly or followed by a slash, so /share matches /share and /share/x but not /share-tips.
_comment_view_url: The ESP-hosted "view in browser" page, which IS the issue when nothing better is found. Deliberately narrower than reject_hosts: list-manage.com is the click-tracking wrapper, so it is rejected as an article link and must never be offered as the public one either. Same shape as the reject pair — a plain host list plus regexes for the numbered hosts.
_comment_tracking: A click-tracking redirect carries its real destination in a query parameter; unwrapping it is what keeps the store's URL key stable. base_tracking_params are stripped from every link; tracking_params are the extra per-recipient parameters stripped from a newsletter link, which RSS callers keep. `utm_`-prefixed keys are matched by prefix in code: a prefix is structure, not vocabulary. workers/rss/src/parse.js keeps a hand-maintained mirror of base_tracking_params.
